messages:
Sophie: Hey team — Escalation from customer (acme-analytics): intermittent 502s from hosted API for large embedding batches (~40MB). Small requests succeed, large fail ~15-30%. Root trace id: 8f3a2c1a. First seen 2026-03-16T18:05:21Z.

Jamal: Can you paste the curl and any headers they used and the edge trace id? :eyes:

Sophie: Curl (sanitized):
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer xxxxx\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  --data-binary @batch_payload.json
```
They rely on chunked Transfer-Encoding (no Content-Length). Failing trace: 8f3a2c1a.

sre-bot: [alert] edge-proxy: spike 502s on host edge-12 (svc-ingress) — 60s window, 18% error rate — started at 2026-03-16T18:04:40Z

Mauro: Sounds like proxy buffer / upstream close on chunked bodies. nginx + chunked + big responses can hit \"upstream prematurely closed connection\" during flush. Can we grab nginx ingress logs and envoy/edge traces?

Sophie: nginx error excerpt for 8f3a2c1a (sanitized):
```
2026/03/16 18:05:21 [error] 12345#0: *987654 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.1.2.3, server: api.redwood.ai, request: \"POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/1.1\", upstream: \"http://10.2.3.4:8080/\", host: \"api.redwood.ai\", referrer: \"-\"
```
Also saw `recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer)` and `upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out)` lines.

Devon: Upstream runtime is on dedicated hosts; if runtime closed socket mid-response we'd expect OOM or trace in worker logs. Runtime team: can you tail worker logs around this ts and report p99 latency/CPU?

Mauro: Two hypotheses: (1) runtime OOM when handling large KV/cache allocations, or (2) proxy buffering + chunked flush causing upstream to block and then connection reset. For (2), nginx default proxy_buffers might be too small for huge JSON arrays; app writes then blocks and kernel RST happens.

Jamal: Repro suggestions: force chunked (no Content-Length) and then set Content-Length to compare. Example:
```
# chunked (no Content-Length)
curl -v -H \"Transfer-Encoding: chunked\" --data-binary @large.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings

# non-chunked (set Content-Length)
SIZE=$(wc -c < large.json); curl -v -H \"Content-Length: $SIZE\" --data-binary @large.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
```

Sophie: Ran tests against edge-12. Chunked: 7/20 failed. Content-Length: 1/20 failed. Points to proxy/streaming interaction. :thinking_face:

Mauro: Immediate mitigations: increase nginx `proxy_buffers` and `proxy_busy_buffers_size` on ingress; or `proxy_request_buffering off;` for this route if downstream supports streaming; ask clients to set Content-Length / smaller batches short-term.

Devon: Runtime logs show no OOMs; process wrote response but kernel showed TCP RST with source IP = ingress around same time. That points to proxy side dropping connection or keepalive/timeout behavior.

Jamal: Let's tcpdump on edge-12 for failing trace to confirm RST timing:
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.2.3.4 and port 8080 -w /tmp/trace-8f3a2c1a.pcap
```
Also capture nginx vars for request: `$upstream_status`, `$upstream_response_time`, `$request_time`.

Sophie: access.log excerpt (8f3a2c1a):
```
8f3a2c1a - - [16/Mar/2026:18:05:21 +0000] \"POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/1.1\" 502 173 \"-\" \"curl/7.82.0\" \"-\" \"-\" \"0.238\" \"1.024\" \"0.03\"
```
Some lines show `upstream_response_time` split values like `0.24, 0.78`.

Mauro: Split upstream times -> upstream did partial writes then closed. Config plan: bump `proxy_buffers` from default (8 4k) to `32 16k` and `proxy_busy_buffers_size 64k`. Stage on edge-12 first.

sre-bot: [change] Rolling canary nginx config increase on edge-12 scheduled — change-id: cfg-2026-03-16-emb-buf-01

Jamal: Before rollout, run staging with same nginx build. Who can run staging?

Mauro: Running staging now with:
```
proxy_buffers 32 16k;
proxy_busy_buffers_size 64k;
proxy_read_timeout 120s;
```
Re-running chunked/non-chunked curl tests.

Sophie: Customer will temporarily reduce batch size and set Content-Length for critical flows. They asked ETA for fix.

Mauro: Staging results: chunked failure down from ~35% -> 2% with buffer changes. Non-chunked stays healthy. No staging CPU/memory regressions. Plan: canary edge-12 for 30m then roll to same-AZ edges.

Devon: Recommend `proxy_read_timeout 120s` to cover heavy encode/decode times; also verify keepalive settings between nginx and upstream.

Jamal: I'll coordinate canary rollout, monitor p50/p95/p99 and 502 rate, and prepare rollback. Any objections?

support-eng: No objections. ETA to customer: 60-90 minutes for canary + verification, 3 hours for global roll.

Sophie: Customer updated and applying temporary mitigations. Thanks all. :raised_hands:

sre-bot: [metric] post-change: edge-12 502 rate dropped to ~2% in canary after buffer change — monitoring.

Jamal: Follow-ups: (1) add synthetic test for chunked large payloads in ingress smoke, (2) docs recommending Content-Length for large batches, (3) consider default buffer increases if recurring.

support-eng: Filed ticket INT-2521 (chunked payload smoke test, docs, config review).

Sophie: Closing thread — will reopen if reoccurs or customer reports. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
